Robust Yeo-Johnson Transformation Recipe Step

Source: R/recipe_steps_robust.R
step_robust_yeojohnson.Rd

step_robust_yeojohnson() creates a specification of a recipe step that transforms the selected variables toward central normality with the robust Yeo-Johnson transformation of robust_yeojohnson(). It is the robust counterpart of recipes::step_YeoJohnson().

Usage

step_robust_yeojohnson(
  recipe,
  ...,
  role = NA,
  trained = FALSE,
  quantile = 0.99,
  nbsteps = 2,
  standardize = TRUE,
  res = NULL,
  columns = NULL,
  skip = FALSE,
  id = recipes::rand_id("robust_yeojohnson")
)

Arguments

recipe

A recipe object. The step will be added to the sequence of operations for this recipe.

...

One or more selector functions to choose the predictors (for example, the spectral channels). See recipes::selections().

role

Not used by this step, since no new variables are created.

trained

A logical indicating whether the step has been trained.

quantile

The quantile of the absolute value of a standard normal variable beyond which the standardized transformed values are given weight zero in the re-weighting steps, strictly between 0 and 1. Default is 0.99.

nbsteps

The number of re-weighting steps, a positive integer. Default is 2.

standardize

A logical value: standardize the transformed variables by the mean and standard deviation of the inliers (TRUE, default).

res

The fitted transformation, stored once the step has been trained.

columns

The names of the selected columns, stored once the step has been trained.

skip

A logical. Should the step be skipped when the recipe is baked by recipes::bake()? Keep the default FALSE, so that new data are corrected with the same filter as the training data.

id

A character string that is unique to this step.

Value

An updated version of recipe with the new step added to the sequence of existing steps.

Details

The transformation parameter \(\lambda\) of each variable is estimated on the training data (Raymaekers and Rousseeuw, 2021), as in robust_yeojohnson(), and applied unchanged to new data. With standardize = TRUE, the transformed variables are also centered and scaled with the mean and standard deviation of the training inliers. Variables that cannot be transformed (for example, constant ones) are left unchanged. Missing values are ignored by the fit and stay missing.

tidy() returns a tibble with columns terms, lambda (NA for the variables left unchanged) and id.

See also

robust_yeojohnson(), step_robust_boxcox()

Author

Christian L. Goueguel

Examples

library(recipes)
data(forageLIBS)
spectra <- snv(forageLIBS[-(1:14)])$correction
wl <- as.numeric(names(spectra))
mg <- spectra[which(wl > 279 & wl < 281)]  # the Mg II lines, after SNV
rec <- recipe(~ ., data = mg[1:300, ]) |>
  step_robust_yeojohnson(all_numeric_predictors())
prepped <- prep(rec)
tidy(prepped, number = 1)
